#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound

blocks.text:
Critical finding: at pin bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1, the action's `action.yml` does NOT define a `permissions` input. The valid inputs are: `client-id`, `app-id`, `private-key`, `owner`, `repositories`, `enterprise`, `skip-token-revoke`, `github-api-url`, and the generated `permission-*` inputs (like `permission-contents`).

So the `permissions: contents:write` WITH input (a single `permissions` key with a colon map value) is NOT a valid input at this pin — it gets warned as `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and ignored. The author's round-1 reply claim was RIGHT (the input is ignored), and the PR step comment's claim ("The least-privilege ceiling rides the action's `permissions` input") is WRONG.

The honest fix for Thread 10: the input IS genuinely ignored at this pin. The granular per-permission inputs (e.g. `permission-contents: write`) ARE supported at this pin (the `<START GENERATED PERMISSIONS INPUTS>` block). So the proper least-privilege ceiling can be achieved with `permission-contents: write` instead of `permissions: contents:write`!

Wait — but the reviewer said "verify against the App's delivery logs and fix whichever claim is wrong". Given the action.yml at the pin, the `permissions` input is definitively ignored (not in the input set → GitHub warns "Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'" and the action never reads it). {"patch":"[test/release_flow_race_test.dart#A8C7]
INS.POST 924:
+
+  // ── gh-1561 rework — review threads 8/9/10 ─────────────────────────────
+  // Thread 8: read_published_version() must PROPAGATE failure — a command-
+  // substitution call site drops set -e (inherit_errexit is off), so an
+  // API outage used to read as published="" and could drive classification
+  // (worst case: the re-arm force-push) on NO data at all. Thread 9: the
+  // registration wait's fetch_runs is guarded like the terminal-wait loop
+  // (#1370 doctrine). Thread 10: the mint's least-privilege ceiling must
+  // ride an input the pinned action actually honors.
+  group('gh-1561 rework — pub.dev outage semantics + guarded registration wait', () {
+    test('pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure', () {
+      // Pre-PR semantics restored (thread 8): the top-of-leg read ran in
+      // the main shell under set -e and one failed read exited loudly. The
+      // extracted helper must reproduce that — an outage must never read
+      // as published="" and slip into the behind-classification.
+      final r = runVerify('api-down-top', pubdevApiDown: true);
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.status,
+        isNot('release-in-flight'),
+        reason: 'no data must never masquerade as a neutral skip',
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog,
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the leg dies at the top read — no classification or '
+            'recovery reads on empty data',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)', () {
+      // The headline consequence from review thread 8: with published=""
+      // the old code classified «behind», reached the never-triggered arm
+      // and FORCE-PUSHED the tag purely because the API was unreachable.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-no-rearm',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":777,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"release"}]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        pubdevApiDown: true,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('re-armed')), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'no run-list reads -> no re-arm decision, ever',
+      );
+      // The seeded 2h-backdated tag object is UNTOUCHED — the re-arm (a
+      // state-changing force-push + full ci.yml cascade) never fired.
+      final taggerDate = int.parse(
+        _gitOut([
+          'for-each-ref',
+          'refs/tags/v0.1.497',
+          '--format=%(creatordate:unix)',
+        ], cwd: r.origin),
+      );
+      final actual = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
+        taggerDate * 1000,
+        isUtc: true,
+      );
+      expect(
+        actual.isBefore(
+          DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)),
+        ),
+        isTrue,
+        reason: 'the seeded backdate survives — the re-arm never fired',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip', () {
+      // The second call site (thread 8): the top-of-leg reads serve the
+      // stale replica, the push run is green, then the API drops before the
+      // success-branch re-read — outcome UNOBSERVED, never a false
+      // «publish did not upload» and never a false green.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-success-reread',
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":4242,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"push"}]',
+        curlFailAfterReads: 3,
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('outcome unobserved'));
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('publish did not upload')));
+    });
+
+    test('transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, '
+        'never a dead leg (thread 9)', () {
+      // The 4th branch-list read (the 2nd registration read) fails
+      // transiently — under set -e the unguarded assignment used to kill
+      // the leg exactly when the self-heal was mid-flight.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'rearm-gh-blip',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson: '[]',
+        secondReadJson: '[]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        ghListFailOnRead: 4,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: 'a gh blip must not kill the leg: ${r.output}');
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('was re-armed by this leg'));
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt 2/6)'),
+        reason: r.output,
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        hasLength(8),
+        reason: 'the failed read still consumed its registration attempt',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input '
+        '(thread 10)', () {
+      // Verified against the pinned action (v3.2.0, bcd2ba49): action.yml
+      // defines NO composite `permissions` input (GitHub warns `Unexpected
+      // input(s) 'permissions'` and the action never reads it — the
+      // round-1 author reply was right), but it DOES define the generated
+      // `permission-*` inputs, which the action turns into the mint
+      // request's permissions map. The ceiling must ride the honored input.
+      final daily = read('.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml');
+      final mintAt = daily.indexOf('actions/create-github-app-token@');
+      expect(
+        mintAt,
+        greaterThan(-1),
+        reason: 'the pubdev leg mints the re-arm token',
+      );
+      final mintEnd = daily.indexOf('- name: Verify pub.dev', mintAt);
+      expect(mintEnd, greaterThan(mintAt));
+      final mintBlock = daily.substring(mintAt, mintEnd);
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        contains('permission-contents: write'),
+        reason: 'the least-privilege ceiling (contents:write — the tag '
+            're-push) must come from the honored input',
+      );
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        isNot(contains(RegExp(r'^\s*permissions:', multiLine: true))),
+        reason: 'the composite `permissions` key is dead at this pin — '
+            'keeping it would overclaim a ceiling that does not exist',
+      );
+    });
+  });"}

# pr-1566: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push

## Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi
  echo "$a"
}

# gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG — the committed
# pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder. The `pubspec=` output key name is
# kept (daily-publish report consumers read it), its value is the tag
# version. No remote tags → nothing has ever been released → up-to-date.
latest_remote_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v*' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -v '\^' | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's|refs/tags/||' \
  | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
pubspec="${latest_remote_tag#v}"
emit "pubspec=$pubspec"
emit "published=" # re-exported below after query

if grep -q '^publish_to: *none' pubspec.yaml; then
  emit "status=private"
  echo "::notice::pubspec declares publish_to: none — package is private, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$pubspec" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::no vX.Y.Z tags on the remote — nothing has been released yet, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

# pub.dev API reads lag minutes behind a fresh publish (CDN replicas) — a
# single stale read must not send us into recovery. Three spaced reads, take
# the newest by version. Fails (non-zero) when the API is unreachable —
# callers decide whether that is fatal.
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}

published=""
published=$(read_published_version)
emit "published=$published"
echo "pubspec=$pubspec published=$published"
newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
if [ "$newest" = "$published" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::pub.dev already serves $published"
  exit 0
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# gh-1561: re-arm a tag whose push twin never fired. Recreate the annotated
# tag object on the SAME commit (new tagger date -> new oid -> the ref
# update fires a real tag-push event, which a same-oid push never would)
# and force-push it with the App token. The commit is read from the remote
# tag and pushed back unchanged — the re-arm never moves what the tag
# points at, only re-announces it. RELEASE_APP_PUSH_URL overrides the push
# destination (test seam; production derives it from RELEASE_APP_TOKEN).

**Fix** (in `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`):
```bash
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt ok=1
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version'); then
      ok=0
    fi
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  [ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}
```

Plan of edits to `test/release_flow_race_test.dart`:

1. curl stub: add `curl-fail-after` seam (after the curl-fail block).
2. gh stub list arm: add `gh-list-fail-on` seam (after counter increment).
3. `runVerify` params: `pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead`.
4. New group with the 5 new tests:

     a. `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` (RED: current exits 0 in-flight).
     b. `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` (RED: current re-arms + in-flight 0).
     c. `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` (green pin for the second call site).
     d. `transient gh failure inside the registration wait reads as still-pending` (RED: current dies set -e exit 1).
     e. wiring: `the pubdev mint's least-privilege ceiling rides the working granular input` (RED: current has dead `permissions:` key, no `permission-contents`).

For (b): the tag-re-cut assertion — after fix, origin tag remains backdated. Compute taggerDate on r.origin via _gitOut for-each-ref — same as existing test. Assert `actual.isBefore(now.subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)))` is TRUE (still the seeded 2h-backdate; not re-cut). Before fix it'd be false (re-cut fresh). Wait — before fix, the leg re-arms and exits 0 in-flight — my assertions `exitCode isNot(0)` fails first. Dart's expect reports all failures though (multiple failures get collected... actually expect throws on first failure per test by default? package:test collects multiple failures in one test body — no, it throws at the first failing expect; subsequent expects don't run). Doesn't matter — RED is RED.

For (b) setup: tagAge 2h, runsJson = release-only completed run, rearmPushTo 'origin', RELEASE_APP_TOKEN stub, pubdevApiDown true. After fix: exit ≠ 0, '::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify', errored, output isNot contains('re-armed'), tag still backdated, and ghLog branch reads empty (leg died before classification reads).

Hmm wait — after the fix, will the leg exit BEFORE fetch_runs? The top-of-leg read happens before `tag=` is even set... yes: pubspec/published comparison → exit 1. But `git ls-remote --tags` happened (real git). gh stub never called → r.ghLog empty. 

For (a): young tag default (60s), runsJson '[]', pubdevApiDown. After fix: exit ≠ 0 + message + errored + ghLog empty + status not 'release-in-flight' (outputs status would be... on exit 1 before any emit status, outputs has pubspec=0.1.497 and published= (empty). r.status = '' → expect r.status, isNot('release-in-flight')). Also output isNot contains('release in flight').

For (c): setup — top-of-leg must serve stale: curl works for reads 1-3 (serving 0.1.496), then fails. curlFailAfterReads: 3. runsJson: completed success push (databaseId 4242). Expect: exit 0, inFlight true, errored false, output contains 'pub.dev API is unreachable — outcome unobserved', isNot contains('publish did not upload'). This is GREEN before AND after (pins the contract). To make it slightly stronger after the fix: the `|| fresh=""` — can't be observed differently. Fine.

Wait — actually there IS an observable difference before/after for (c): none. It's a pin. OK.

But hold on — (c) with curlFailAfterReads BEFORE the fix: read_published_version returns acc of... reads 4,5,6 fail; acc collects ""s → fresh="" → -z → in_flight. Same. Yes.

For (d): tagAge 2h, runsJson '[]', secondReadJson '[]', rearmPushTo 'origin', RELEASE_APP_TOKEN stub, ghListFailOnRead: 4. After fix: exit 0, inFlight, errored false, contains 'was re-armed by this leg', contains 'transient gh failure reading the run list', branch reads hasLength(8). Before fix: script dies at read 4 (set -e) → exit 1. RED.

Hmm — one check on (d) before-fix behavior: `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` fails → set -e kills → GITHUB_OUTPUT has pubspec + published(0.1.496 stale) + no status. exitCode 1. RED confirmed on `expect(r.exitCode, 0)`.

For (e): string-slice assertions on daily-publish.yml. RED before (no permission-contents; dead permissions key present), GREEN after.

With the `||` handler, published="" initialization is redundant but harmless; actually with `published=$(...)` the var gets set even on failure. The reviewer's suggested snippet drops it? Their snippet: `published=$(read_published_version) || { ...; exit 1; }`. Keep the shape clean:

```bash
published=$(read_published_version) ||
  { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }
```

Hmm, style: the file uses one-line `if` bodies etc. I'll write:

```bash
# gh-1561 rework (review thread 8): the pre-PR inline loop ran in the main
# shell under set -e — one failed read exited the leg loudly. A command-
# substitution call site drops that guard (inherit_errexit is off), so the
# helper propagates the all-reads-failed case itself and each caller
# decides: the top of the leg is fatal (no data must never classify, never
# drive rerun/re-arm recovery), the success branch treats it as unobserved.
published=$(read_published_version) || {
  echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"
  exit 1
}
```

And drop the now-dead `published=""` line above it.

The function:

```bash
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt ok=1
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version'); then
      ok=0
    fi
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  # A command-substitution subshell does not inherit set -e (inherit_errexit
  # is off): return the failure explicitly, never fall off the printf.
  [ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}
```

Success branch:

```

Registration wait:
```bash
    while [ "$attempt" -le "$registration_reads" ]; do
      sleep "$read_sleep"
      # Same doctrine as the terminal-wait loop (#1370): a transient gh
      # failure reads as «still pending» — it must never kill the leg under
      # set -e (review thread 9). The failed read still consumes the attempt.
      if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then
        echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"
        attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
        continue
      fi
      tag_run=$(push_run_of "$runs_json")
      [ -n "$tag_run" ] && break
      attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
    done
```

{"patch":"[test/release_flow_race_test.dart#A8C7]

+
+  // ── gh-1561 rework — review threads 8/9/10 ─────────────────────────────
+  // Thread 8: read_published_version() must PROPAGATE failure — a command-
+  // substitution call site drops set -e (inherit_errexit is off), so an
+  // API outage used to read as published="" and could drive classification
+  // (worst case: the re-arm force-push) on NO data at all. Thread 9: the
+  // registration wait's fetch_runs is guarded like the terminal-wait loop
+  // (#1370 doctrine). Thread 10: the mint's least-privilege ceiling must
+  // ride an input the pinned action actually honors.
+  group('gh-1561 rework — pub.dev outage semantics + guarded registration wait', () {
+    test('pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure', () {
+      // Pre-PR semantics restored (thread 8): the top-of-leg read ran in
+      // the main shell under set -e and one failed read exited loudly. The
+      // extracted helper must reproduce that — an outage must never read
+      // as published="" and slip into the behind-classification.
+      final r = runVerify('api-down-top', pubdevApiDown: true);
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.status,
+        isNot('release-in-flight'),
+        reason: 'no data must never masquerade as a neutral skip',
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog,
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the leg dies at the top read — no classification or '
+            'recovery reads on empty data',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)', () {
+      // The headline consequence from review thread 8: with published=""
+      // the old code classified «behind», reached the never-triggered arm
+      // and FORCE-PUSHED the tag purely because the API was unreachable.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-no-rearm',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":777,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"release"}]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        pubdevApiDown: true,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('re-armed')), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'no run-list reads -> no re-arm decision, ever',
+      );
+      // The seeded 2h-backdated tag object is UNTOUCHED — the re-arm (a
+      // state-changing force-push + full ci.yml cascade) never fired.
+      final taggerDate = int.parse(
+        _gitOut([
+          'for-each-ref',
+          'refs/tags/v0.1.497',
+          '--format=%(creatordate:unix)',
+        ], cwd: r.origin),
+      );
+      final actual = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
+        taggerDate * 1000,
+        isUtc: true,
+      );
+      expect(
+        actual.isBefore(
+          DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)),
+        ),
+        isTrue,
+        reason: 'the seeded backdate survives — the re-arm never fired',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip', () {
+      // The second call site (thread 8): the top-of-leg reads serve the
+      // stale replica, the push run is green, then the API drops before the
+      // success-branch re-read — outcome UNOBSERVED, never a false
+      // «publish did not upload» and never a false green.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-success-reread',
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":4242,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"push"}]',
+        curlFailAfterReads: 3,
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('outcome unobserved'));
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('publish did not upload')));
+    });
+
+    test('transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, '
+        'never a dead leg (thread 9)', () {
+      // The 4th branch-list read (the 2nd registration read) fails
+      // transiently — under set -e the unguarded assignment used to kill
+      // the leg exactly when the self-heal was mid-flight.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'rearm-gh-blip',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson: '[]',
+        secondReadJson: '[]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        ghListFailOnRead: 4,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: 'a gh blip must not kill the leg: ${r.output}');
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('was re-armed by this leg'));
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt 2/6)'),
+        reason: r.output,
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        hasLength(8),
+        reason: 'the failed read still consumed its registration attempt',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input '
+        '(thread 10)', () {
+      // Verified against the pinned action (v3.2.0, bcd2ba49): action.yml
+      // defines NO composite `permissions` input (GitHub warns `Unexpected
+      // input(s) 'permissions'` and the action never reads it — the
+      // round-1 author reply was right), but it DOES define the generated
+      // `permission-*` inputs, which the action turns into the mint
+      // request's permissions map. The ceiling must ride the honored input.
+      final daily = read('.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml');
+      final mintAt = daily.indexOf('actions/create-github-app-token@');
+      expect(
+        mintAt,
+        greaterThan(-1),

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi
  echo "$a"
}

# gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG — the committed
# pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder. The `pubspec=` output key name is
# kept (daily-publish report consumers read it), its value is the tag
# version. No remote tags → nothing has ever been released → up-to-date.
latest_remote_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v*' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -v '\^' | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's|refs/tags/||' \
  | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
pubspec="${latest_remote_tag#v}"
emit "pubspec=$pubspec"
emit "published=" # re-exported below after query

if grep -q '^publish_to: *none' pubspec.yaml; then
  emit "status=private"
  echo "::notice::pubspec declares publish_to: none — package is private, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$pubspec" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::no vX.Y.Z tags on the remote — nothing has been released yet, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

# pub.dev API reads lag minutes behind a fresh publish (CDN replicas) — a
# single stale read must not send us into recovery. Three spaced reads, take
# the newest by version. Fails (non-zero) when the API is unreachable —
# callers decide whether that is fatal.
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}

published=""
published=$(read_published_version)

read_published_version() {

{"patch":"[test/release_flow_race_test.dart#A8C7]
INS.POST 924:
+
+  // ── gh-1561 rework — review threads 8/9/10 ─────────────────────────────
+  // Thread 8: read_published_version() must PROPAGATE failure — a command-
+  // substitution call site drops set -e (inherit_errexit is off), so an
+  // API outage used to read as published="" and could drive classification
+  // (worst case: the re-arm force-push) on NO data at all. Thread 9: the
+  // registration wait's fetch_runs is guarded like the terminal-wait loop
+  // (#1370 doctrine). Thread 10: the mint's least-privilege ceiling must
+  // ride an input the pinned action actually honors.
+  group('gh-1561 rework — pub.dev outage semantics + guarded registration wait', () {
+    test('pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure', () {
+      // Pre-PR semantics restored (thread 8): the top-of-leg read ran in
+      // the main shell under set -e and one failed read exited loudly. The
+      // extracted helper must reproduce that — an outage must never read
+      // as published="" and slip into the behind-classification.
+      final r = runVerify('api-down-top', pubdevApiDown: true);
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.status,
+        isNot('release-in-flight'),
+        reason: 'no data must never masquerade as a neutral skip',
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog,
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the leg dies at the top read — no classification or '
+            'recovery reads on empty data',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)', () {
+      // The headline consequence from review thread 8: with published=""
+      // the old code classified «behind», reached the never-triggered arm
+      // and FORCE-PUSHED the tag purely because the API was unreachable.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-no-rearm',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":777,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"release"}]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        pubdevApiDown: true,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('re-armed')), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'no run-list reads -> no re-arm decision, ever',
+      );
+      // The seeded 2h-backdated tag object is UNTOUCHED — the re-arm (a
+      // state-changing force-push + full ci.yml cascade) never fired.
+      final taggerDate = int.parse(
+        _gitOut([
+          'for-each-ref',
+          'refs/tags/v0.1.497',
+          '--format=%(creatordate:unix)',
+        ], cwd: r.origin),
+      );
+      final actual = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
+        taggerDate * 1000,
+        isUtc: true,
+      );
+      expect(
+        actual.isBefore(
+          DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)),
+        ),
+        isTrue,
+        reason: 'the seeded backdate survives — the re-arm never fired',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip', () {
+      // The second call site (thread 8): the top-of-leg reads serve the
+      // stale replica, the push run is green, then the API drops before the
+      // success-branch re-read — outcome UNOBSERVED, never a false
+      // «publish did not upload» and never a false green.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-success-reread',
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":4242,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"push"}]',
+        curlFailAfterReads: 3,
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('outcome unobserved'));
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('publish did not upload')));
+    });
+
+    test('transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, '
+        'never a dead leg (thread 9)', () {
+      // The 4th branch-list read (the 2nd registration read) fails
+      // transiently — under set -e the unguarded assignment used to kill
+      // the leg exactly when the self-heal was mid-flight.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'rearm-gh-blip',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson: '[]',
+        secondReadJson: '[]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        ghListFailOnRead: 4,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: 'a gh blip must not kill the leg: ${r.output}');
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('was re-armed by this leg'));
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt 2/6)'),
+        reason: r.output,
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        hasLength(8),
+        reason: 'the failed read still consumed its registration attempt',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input '
+        '(thread 10)', () {
+      // Verified against the pinned action (v3.2.0, bcd2ba49): action.yml
+      // defines NO composite `permissions` input (GitHub warns `Unexpected
+      // input(s) 'permissions'` and the action never reads it — the
+      // round-1 author reply was right), but it DOES define the generated
+      // `permission-*` inputs, which the action turns into the mint
+      // request's permissions map. The ceiling must ride the honored input.
+      final daily = read('.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml');
+      final mintAt = daily.indexOf('actions/create-github-app-token@');
+      expect(
+        mintAt,
+        greaterThan(-1),
+        reason: 'the pubdev leg mints the re-arm token',
+      );
+      final mintEnd = daily.indexOf('- name: Verify pub.dev', mintAt);
+      expect(mintEnd, greaterThan(mintAt));
+      final mintBlock = daily.substring(mintAt, mintEnd);
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        contains('permission-contents: write'),
+        reason: 'the least-privilege ceiling (contents:write — the tag '
+            're-push) must come from the honored input',
+      );
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        isNot(contains(RegExp(r'^\s*permissions:', multiLine: true))),
+        reason: 'the composite `permissions` key is dead at this pin — '
+            'keeping it would overclaim a ceiling that does not exist',
+      );
+    });
+  });"}

# Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). No inputs to disambiguate on
          # (newest-in-tight-window fallback), watch bounded at 60m =
          # child worst-case 45m (#351) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 3600 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent exactly (ci.yml release
      # job, the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change. The
      # least-privilege ceiling rides the action's `permissions` input
      # (contents:write covers the tag re-push), identical to the precedent.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues

{"patch":"[test/release_flow_race_test.dart#A8C7]
INS.POST 924:
+
+  // ── gh-1561 rework — review threads 8/9/10 ─────────────────────────────
+  // Thread 8: read_published_version() must PROPAGATE failure — a command-
+  // substitution call site drops set -e (inherit_errexit is off), so an
+  // API outage used to read as published="" and could drive classification
+  // (worst case: the re-arm force-push) on NO data at all. Thread 9: the
+  // registration wait's fetch_runs is guarded like the terminal-wait loop
+  // (#1370 doctrine). Thread 10: the mint's least-privilege ceiling must
+  // ride an input the pinned action actually honors.
+  group('gh-1561 rework — pub.dev outage semantics + guarded registration wait', () {
+    test('pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure', () {
+      // Pre-PR semantics restored (thread 8): the top-of-leg read ran in
+      // the main shell under set -e and one failed read exited loudly. The
+      // extracted helper must reproduce that — an outage must never read
+      // as published="" and slip into the behind-classification.
+      final r = runVerify('api-down-top', pubdevApiDown: true);
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.status,
+        isNot('release-in-flight'),
+        reason: 'no data must never masquerade as a neutral skip',
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog,
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the leg dies at the top read — no classification or '
+            'recovery reads on empty data',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)', () {
+      // The headline consequence from review thread 8: with published=""
+      // the old code classified «behind», reached the never-triggered arm
+      // and FORCE-PUSHED the tag purely because the API was unreachable.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-no-rearm',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":777,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"release"}]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        pubdevApiDown: true,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('re-armed')), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'no run-list reads -> no re-arm decision, ever',
+      );
+      // The seeded 2h-backdated tag object is UNTOUCHED — the re-arm (a
+      // state-changing force-push + full ci.yml cascade) never fired.
+      final taggerDate = int.parse(
+        _gitOut([
+          'for-each-ref',
+          'refs/tags/v0.1.497',
+          '--format=%(creatordate:unix)',
+        ], cwd: r.origin),
+      );
+      final actual = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
+        taggerDate * 1000,
+        isUtc: true,
+      );
+      expect(
+        actual.isBefore(
+          DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)),
+        ),
+        isTrue,
+        reason: 'the seeded backdate survives — the re-arm never fired',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip', () {
+      // The second call site (thread 8): the top-of-leg reads serve the
+      // stale replica, the push run is green, then the API drops before the
+      // success-branch re-read — outcome UNOBSERVED, never a false
+      // «publish did not upload» and never a false green.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-success-reread',
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":4242,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"push"}]',
+        curlFailAfterReads: 3,
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('outcome unobserved'));
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('publish did not upload')));
+    });
+
+    test('transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, '
+        'never a dead leg (thread 9)', () {
+      // The 4th branch-list read (the 2nd registration read) fails
+      // transiently — under set -e the unguarded assignment used to kill
+      // the leg exactly when the self-heal was mid-flight.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'rearm-gh-blip',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson: '[]',
+        secondReadJson: '[]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        ghListFailOnRead: 4,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: 'a gh blip must not kill the leg: ${r.output}');
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('was re-armed by this leg'));
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt 2/6)'),
+        reason: r.output,
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        hasLength(8),
+        reason: 'the failed read still consumed its registration attempt',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input '
+        '(thread 10)', () {
+      // Verified against the pinned action (v3.2.0, bcd2ba49): action.yml
+      // defines NO composite `permissions` input (GitHub warns `Unexpected
+      // input(s) 'permissions'` and the action never reads it — the
+      // round-1 author reply was right), but it DOES define the generated
+      // `permission-*` inputs, which the action turns into the mint
+      // request's permissions map. The ceiling must ride the honored input.
+      final daily = read('.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml');
+      final mintAt = daily.indexOf('actions/create-github-app-token@');
+      expect(
+        mintAt,
+        greaterThan(-1),
+        reason: 'the pubdev leg mints the re-arm token',
+      );
+      final mintEnd = daily.indexOf('- name: Verify pub.dev', mintAt);
+      expect(mintEnd, greaterThan(mintAt));
+      final mintBlock = daily.substring(mintAt, mintEnd);
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        contains('permission-contents: write'),
+        reason: 'the least-privilege ceiling (contents:write — the tag '
+            're-push) must come from the honored input',
+      );
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        isNot(contains(RegExp(r'^\s*permissions:', multiLine: true))),
+        reason: 'the composite `permissions` key is dead at this pin — '
+            'keeping it would overclaim a ceiling that does not exist',
+      );
+    });
+  });"}

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent exactly (ci.yml release
      # job, the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change. The
      # least-privilege ceiling rides the action's `permissions` input
      # (contents:write covers the tag re-push), identical to the precedent.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues

{"patch":"[test/release_flow_race_test.dart#A8C7]
INS.POST 924:
+
+  // ── gh-1561 rework — review threads 8/9/10 ─────────────────────────────
+  // Thread 8: read_published_version() must PROPAGATE failure — a command-
+  // substitution call site drops set -e (inherit_errexit is off), so an
+  // API outage used to read as published="" and could drive classification
+  // (worst case: the re-arm force-push) on NO data at all. Thread 9: the
+  // registration wait's fetch_runs is guarded like the terminal-wait loop
+  // (#1370 doctrine). Thread 10: the mint's least-privilege ceiling must
+  // ride an input the pinned action actually honors.
+  group('gh-1561 rework — pub.dev outage semantics + guarded registration wait', () {
+    test('pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure', () {
+      // Pre-PR semantics restored (thread 8): the top-of-leg read ran in
+      // the main shell under set -e and one failed read exited loudly. The
+      // extracted helper must reproduce that — an outage must never read
+      // as published="" and slip into the behind-classification.
+      final r = runVerify('api-down-top', pubdevApiDown: true);
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.status,
+        isNot('release-in-flight'),
+        reason: 'no data must never masquerade as a neutral skip',
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog,
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the leg dies at the top read — no classification or '
+            'recovery reads on empty data',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)', () {
+      // The headline consequence from review thread 8: with published=""
+      // the old code classified «behind», reached the never-triggered arm
+      // and FORCE-PUSHED the tag purely because the API was unreachable.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-no-rearm',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":777,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"release"}]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        pubdevApiDown: true,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, isNot(0), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify'),
+      );
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('re-armed')), reason: r.output);
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'no run-list reads -> no re-arm decision, ever',
+      );
+      // The seeded 2h-backdated tag object is UNTOUCHED — the re-arm (a
+      // state-changing force-push + full ci.yml cascade) never fired.
+      final taggerDate = int.parse(
+        _gitOut([
+          'for-each-ref',
+          'refs/tags/v0.1.497',
+          '--format=%(creatordate:unix)',
+        ], cwd: r.origin),
+      );
+      final actual = DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
+        taggerDate * 1000,
+        isUtc: true,
+      );
+      expect(
+        actual.isBefore(
+          DateTime.now().toUtc().subtract(const Duration(minutes: 90)),
+        ),
+        isTrue,
+        reason: 'the seeded backdate survives — the re-arm never fired',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip', () {
+      // The second call site (thread 8): the top-of-leg reads serve the
+      // stale replica, the push run is green, then the API drops before the
+      // success-branch re-read — outcome UNOBSERVED, never a false
+      // «publish did not upload» and never a false green.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'api-down-success-reread',
+        runsJson:
+            '[{"databaseId":4242,"status":"completed","conclusion":"success","event":"push"}]',
+        curlFailAfterReads: 3,
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('outcome unobserved'));
+      expect(r.output, isNot(contains('publish did not upload')));
+    });
+
+    test('transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, '
+        'never a dead leg (thread 9)', () {
+      // The 4th branch-list read (the 2nd registration read) fails
+      // transiently — under set -e the unguarded assignment used to kill
+      // the leg exactly when the self-heal was mid-flight.
+      final r = runVerify(
+        'rearm-gh-blip',
+        tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+        runsJson: '[]',
+        secondReadJson: '[]',
+        rearmPushTo: 'origin',
+        ghListFailOnRead: 4,
+        extraEnv: const {'RELEASE_APP_TOKEN': 'stub-token'},
+      );
+      expect(r.exitCode, 0, reason: 'a gh blip must not kill the leg: ${r.output}');
+      expect(r.inFlight, isTrue, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.errored, isFalse, reason: r.output);
+      expect(r.output, contains('was re-armed by this leg'));
+      expect(
+        r.output,
+        contains('transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt 2/6)'),
+        reason: r.output,
+      );
+      expect(
+        r.ghLog.where((l) => l.contains('--branch v0.1.497')),
+        hasLength(8),
+        reason: 'the failed read still consumed its registration attempt',
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input '
+        '(thread 10)', () {
+      // Verified against the pinned action (v3.2.0, bcd2ba49): action.yml
+      // defines NO composite `permissions` input (GitHub warns `Unexpected
+      // input(s) 'permissions'` and the action never reads it — the
+      // round-1 author reply was right), but it DOES define the generated
+      // `permission-*` inputs, which the action turns into the mint
+      // request's permissions map. The ceiling must ride the honored input.
+      final daily = read('.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml');
+      final mintAt = daily.indexOf('actions/create-github-app-token@');
+      expect(
+        mintAt,
+        greaterThan(-1),
+        reason: 'the pubdev leg mints the re-arm token',
+      );
+      final mintEnd = daily.indexOf('- name: Verify pub.dev', mintAt);
+      expect(mintEnd, greaterThan(mintAt));
+      final mintBlock = daily.substring(mintAt, mintEnd);
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        contains('permission-contents: write'),
+        reason: 'the least-privilege ceiling (contents:write — the tag '
+            're-push) must come from the honored input',
+      );
+      expect(
+        mintBlock,
+        isNot(contains(RegExp(r'^\s*permissions:', multiLine: true))),
+        reason: 'the composite `permissions` key is dead at this pin — '
+            'keeping it would overclaim a ceiling that does not exist',
+      );
+    });
+  });"}
