# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)

#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with

# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)

#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof

# green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded

Fixed in `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — the helper now propagates failure and each caller decides, exactly per the suggested shape:

```bash
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt ok=1
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version'); then
      ok=0
    fi
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  [ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}
```

- **Top of the leg — pre-PR loud failure restored**: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }`. An outage now exits before any classification — it can no longer reach the behind-branch, so `gh run rerun --failed` and the `rearm_tag()` force-push can never fire on empty data.
- **Success branch — neutral skip kept**: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard then takes the unobserved-in-flight path.
- The `ok` flag lives **inside** the subshell (a `return 1` propagates through `$( )`), which is why the flag-based shape is used instead of relying on `set -e` — the exact mechanism your verification identified.

**Tests** (TDD, all reproducing red before the fix): the `curl-fail` seam is now wired into `runVerify` as `pubdevApiDown`, plus a `curlFailAfterReads` seam for a mid-leg outage:

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — asserts the `::error::` text, non-zero exit, and **zero gh reads** (no classification/recovery reads on empty data).
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm` — release-twin fixture + re-arm credential available + API down: the leg must die at the top read and the seeded tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here — the headline consequence).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` (`curlFailAfterReads: 3`) — pins the second call site: unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov

read_published_version() {

#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are

#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.
- `wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input (thread 10)` — asserts `permission-contents: write` present and no dead `permissions:` key inside the mint step.

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.
- `wiring: the pubdev mint ceiling rides the WORKING granular input (thread 10)` — asserts `permission-contents: write` present and no dead `permissions:` key inside the mint step.

    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:

    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded

    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty

    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.

#              + junit durations (core/shared)

#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)

concurrency:

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   installer-portability → gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the POSIX-dialect proof
#               for the first-run wizard (site/** or the generator
#               touched) — dash + busybox ash on ubuntu, bash on macOS;
#               red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"content":"# PR #1566 rework — review threads 8, 9, 10 fixed

## Issues/Notes

Three open review threads, all addressed with code fixes (TDD — every fix was red first, then green):

- **Thread 8 (IMPORTANT)** — `read_published_version()` never failed: a command-substitution subshell drops `set -e` (`inherit_errexit` off) and the function's last command was `printf`, so a full pub.dev outage yielded `published=""` and the leg slid into the behind-classification on no data — able to fire `gh run rerun --failed` or the `rearm_tag()` force-push purely because the API was unreachable.
- **Thread 9 (IMPORTANT)** — the re-arm registration wait called `runs_json=$(fetch_runs)` unguarded in the main shell: one transient `gh` blip killed the leg under `set -e` mid-self-heal, against the file's own #1370 doctrine.
- **Thread 10 (SUGGESTION)** — the two claims about the mint's `permissions` input were contradictory. Verified against the pinned action (`v3.2.0`, `bcd2ba49`): `action.yml` defines **no** composite `permissions` input (it warns `Unexpected input(s) 'permissions'` and never reads it — the round-1 author reply was right), but it **does** define generated `permission-*` inputs which `lib/get-permissions-from-inputs.js` turns into the mint request's permissions map. The PR comment overclaimed a ceiling that did not exist.

## Approach

- **Thread 8** — `read_published_version()` now tracks an `ok` flag (`[ "$ok" -eq 0 ] || return 1`); call sites decide:
  - top of the leg: `published=$(read_published_version) || { echo "::error::pub.dev API unreachable — cannot classify"; exit 1; }` — pre-PR loud failure restored; an outage can no longer classify, so recovery (rerun/re-arm) is unreachable on empty data;
  - success branch: `fresh=$(read_published_version) || fresh=""` — the existing `[ -z "$fresh" ]` guard keeps the neutral unobserved skip.
- **Thread 9** — the registration wait guards the read exactly like the terminal-wait loop: `if ! runs_json=$(fetch_runs); then echo "transient gh failure reading the run list (attempt $attempt/$registration_reads)"; attempt=…; continue; fi` — the failed read still consumes its attempt, so read-count accounting is unchanged.
- **Thread 10** — the mint step now uses the **honored** granular input, making the least-privilege ceiling real (contents:write only — the tag re-push) instead of documented:

  ```yaml
  - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
    id: app-token
    continue-on-error: true
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      permission-contents: write
  ```

  The step comment now documents the verified mechanism (dead composite input at this pin, honored granular input, inherit-the-installation fallback). Shape otherwise unchanged (same pin, no `if:` — validator, `continue-on-error` failover to the script's manual-re-push alarm).
- **Scope note**: `ci.yml:3980` still passes the dead composite `permissions: contents:write` (pinned by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`); left untouched as out of this PR's flagged scope — noted in the thread-10 reply as a candidate follow-up.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh` — thread 8 (failure propagation + both call sites) and thread 9 (guarded registration wait).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — thread 10 (`permission-contents: write` ceiling + truthful comment).
- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — three new fixture seams (`pubdevApiDown`, `curlFailAfterReads`, `ghListFailOnRead` — the `curl-fail` seam was previously only wired into `runPlan`) and five new tests in a `gh-1561 rework` group.

## Test Coverage

New tests in `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (all verified RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after):

- `pub.dev API down at the top of the leg -> loud classify failure` — `::error::` text, non-zero exit, **zero** gh reads.
- `API outage must never fire the re-arm (no recovery on empty data)` — with the re-arm credential present and a release-twin-only run list, the seeded backdated tag object must remain untouched (the old code re-cut the tag here).
- `pub.dev goes down mid-leg at the success re-read -> neutral skip` — second call site pinned: outcome unobserved, never a false «publish did not upload».
- `transient gh failure inside the registration wait -> still-pending, never a dead leg` — gh blip on the 4th branch-list read; exit 0, in-flight, read count stays 8.
